title: Feasibility of process-based therapy in a naturalistic setting
summary: In the project, we are interested in how psychotherapy can be better tailored to the needs of the person being treated. Despite intensive scientific research, it has not yet been clarified how intensive self-observation can be used to improve psychotherapeutic treatment on the basis of entries in cell phones. This question is being clarified in a study conducted by the Institute of Psychology in cooperation with psychotherapists in private practice by comparing treatment with and without such an intensive self-observation phase. Specifically, we are investigating whether such a procedure in psychotherapy is accepted by patients and practitioners, whether it is feasible and whether better success in symptom reduction can be achieved compared to the routine procedure in psychotherapy.

interventions.name: Interventiongroup: Process-based therapy (Questionnaire input three times per day for 4 weeks; One session per week for 24 weeks)
Controlgroup: Guideline Psychotherapy (One session per week for 24 weeks)

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
The subjects should be willing to participate in outpatient psychotherapy once a week for at least 24 weeks in the respective practice of the participating therapist. For the purpose of the study diagnostics, they have a smartphone and are willing to answer short electronic questionnaires several times a day for at least 4 weeks. You meet the criteria of a depressive disorder or an anxiety disorder. At the start of the study, you are either not receiving any psychiatric medication or your psychiatric medication has been consistent for at least 4 weeks at the start of the study. Due to the transdiagnostic approach, no stricter diagnostic inclusion criteria will be formulated.
Exclusion criteria:
Acute danger to self or others or a suicide attempt in the last six months. Ongoing psychotherapeutic treatment. Current substance dependence, bipolar I disorder (lifetime), psychotic disorder (lifetime), post-traumatic stress disorder, emotionally unstable personality disorder, severe physical illness or mental disorder requiring treatment in another setting (e.g., BMI<18.5, acute psychosis, brain organic disease).
